title: Break The Spin · Nov 26-E (Reich call to nationalize SpaceX)
subtitle: 1 post, real photos (White House Musk; official DOL Reich portrait). Accurate version of a false viral meme, per Scott.

posts.theme: Former Clinton labor secretary calls on Democrats to nationalize SpaceX and Starlink
posts.quote: Clinton's Former Labor Secretary Wants Democrats To Nationalize Elon Musk's SpaceX.
posts.alt: Photo of Elon Musk in the Oval Office, smiling, with American flags behind him. Circle inset of Robert Reich's official Labor Department portrait. Headline text: Clinton's Former Labor Secretary Wants Democrats To Nationalize Elon Musk's SpaceX. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credits: The White House / Molly Riley; official portrait, U.S. Department of Labor.
posts.caption:
Robert Reich was Bill Clinton's labor secretary in the 1990s. He does not hold office now. He still wants the government to take Elon Musk's rocket company.

On his podcast last month, Reich told Democrats to "defund Musk" and start "laying the groundwork for nationalizing Starlink and SpaceX." "Nationalize it," he said. "It should be a public corporation." "We should not ever have that kind of power in one person's hands."

He repeated the call in a column a few days later. If Starlink is so central to the military that the Pentagon cannot cancel the contracts, Reich wrote, "it should be nationalized." He said the project of "defunding Musk" will probably have to wait until after January 20, 2029. On the podcast, he tied that kind of takeover to having "a Democratic administration."

No bill has been introduced. Democratic leaders have not backed his plan. That has not stopped a former Cabinet official from calling for a government takeover of a private American company.

Musk's reply was short: "Stealing companies is a serious crime. Prison for Reich."
posts.first:
The facts: Reich served as U.S. Labor secretary from 1993 to 1997. The remarks were on the Oct. 24, 2026 episode of "The Coffee Klatch with Robert Reich" and in a Guardian column published Oct. 27, 2026. As of Nov. 26, no bill to nationalize SpaceX or Starlink had been introduced, and no Democratic congressional leader had endorsed the idea.

Sources: RealClearPolitics, The Guardian, Fox Business, 24/7 Wall St.
